historical_source: Valizadegan et al ExoMiner++ 2025 TESS 2-minute SPOC S1-S67 labeled event table, 10 originally held-out host folds, published NASA v1.0.0 model out-of-fold scores
unit_of_data: TCE observation row, repeated TCEs from same TIC not independent
split_unit: target_id star, ten published folds, never fit postprocessor on current fold labels
original_model_score: score, released published 10-fold NASA ExoMiner++ prediction; not recomputed, not changed and 2025 model cannot be equated with 2026 v2.4.0
baseline_model: Score-only logistic calibration; input logit(clipped NASA score)
augmented_model: Same logistic calibration plus four published physical measured fields and transit duty cycle
primary_endpoint: Pooled out-of-fold sklearn average_precision_score(augmented) minus average_precision_score(score-only calibration) using identical TIC-disjoint test fold

confidence_interval.method: whole-star paired bootstrap with original TIC as cluster; resample all observations of a star together

scientific_guardrails: Published NASA scores are from the original authors' 2025 cross-validation, not model weights we trained.
Postprocessor training uses published historical labels on other stars, and tests only held-out historical NASA CV folds; this is not untouched exoplanet validation.
More than one sector-run TCE can belong to same TIC and must always be grouped.
No new source features or hyperparameters will be selected after reviewing primary comparison.
Even a reproducible AP gain would be relative to the 2025 released-score reference and not automatically carry over to NASA's 2026 v2.4.0 official pretrained model.
RUWE and transit diagnostics already appear in NASA's advanced original models; do not claim those concepts are new.
Compare baseline calibrated NASA score versus augmented calibration, not merely augmented model versus a weaker four-feature RF.
High score in UNK is not physical planet confirmation.
